flagged.evidence: The Definition says, “if two targets satisfy the same bounds, every coordinate difference is at most 2^{1-b} for all b, hence is zero,” but does not require that they share the same approximant sequence Q_b. For example, I_2 and -I_2 each have an exact rational Cauchy name satisfying the stated error bounds and the same query-time bounds, yet their diagonal real coordinates differ by 2. The estimate follows only for two targets approximated by the same Q_b at every precision.

The page says the examples instantiate “a complete output-error budget.” Its examples list contains four items; ex-qa-37-fibonacci-budget allocates error across QSD factors and says measurement, preparation, Hamiltonian evolution, and phase correction are separate ledger coordinates. It does not state a complete measured-output bound; that result is in lem-qa-37-total-error-budget, which is not listed as an example.
